To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

limitation of cultured hepatoma cells for essential amino acids causes a specific decrease in the functional activity of hepatocyte-specific transcription factors, HNF-1 alpha and HNF-4 alpha, without a change in their DNA binding activities.
the repression of albumin gene expression by amino acid limitation is due to decreased transcriptional activation by the liver-enriching factor, hepatocyte nuclear factors (HNF- 1 and HNF -3).
limitation of essential amino acids in cultured rat hepatoma cell lines causes a specific decrease in the functional activity of HNF1, which in turn results in repression of the serum albumin gene.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism by which the transcription factor, HNF-1, is inactivated by amino acids.
the regulation of gene expression in cultured rat hepatoma (Fao) and human hepatoma (HepG2) cells.
the regulation of liver-specific genes in cultured hepatoma cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the amino acid regulation of albumin and other liver-specific genes occurs through decreased transcriptional activation of the HNFs.

the amino acid regulation of the albumins gene is mediated by a HNF-1 site and a HNF-3 site in the albumins promoter and that this regulation is not mediated by changes in DNA binding activity of the transcription factors.
the amino acid regulation of the albumine promoter is mediated by HNF-3 and HNF-4, and that HNF-3 plays an important role in the amino acid regulation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

amino acid limitation results in decreased transcription by the liver-enriching transcription factors HNF-1, HNF-1alpha and HNF-4, and that this decrease in transcriptional activation by these transcription factors results from decreased activity of the transcriptional activator domains of these factors.
amino acid limitation of hepatoma cells causes a specific decrease in HNF-1 activity and that this decrease is responsible for the repression of the serum albumin gene.
the repression of albumin and HNF- 1 reporter constructs in HepG2 cells is caused specifically by the decreased activity of HNF1.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the HNFs play an essential role in the regulation of liver-specific gene transcription and amino acid regulation of liver-specific genes.
amino acid limitation results in a decrease in transcriptional activity of HNF1, which plays a major role regulating the expression of several liver-specific genes, including the serum protein genes.

amino acid availability is a critical determinant of gene expression in cultured hepatoma cells, and the regulation of gene expression is mediated by transcriptional activators, rather than DNA binding activity.
